content: Since you opened the floodgates of AI assisted fixes, I would like to say that fixing the theories pages in the community pages has been on my to-do list for like nearly a year, and with help from an LLM it should be much quicker. Most of the references to code there are completely stale (an even better fix would be to move them to Verso I guess).
I was planning on taking a stab myself, but if anyone else wants to do it :man_shrugging:
(though maybe a discussion that should be had if the theories pages shouldn't be killed altogether and parts of them maybe perhaps to the phrasebook)
Could you point out to me what you mean by theories pages?
In https://leanprover-community.github.io/ on the left under "Theories"
eg. https://leanprover-community.github.io/theories/topology.html which even has some lean3 is_open :see_no_evil:
the linear algebra one also has a number of stale declarations
Aha, they are incredibly outdated! I think you should go ahead and do it :)
I wonder if people would be interested in having a bootcamp where we spend a whole week cleaning up mathlib :eyes: maybe @Justus Springer ?

Actually maybe, can someone with the power to do so (eg. @Michael Rothgang :pleading_face: ) move the last couple messages to another thread? I guess this is something where getting the collective opinion on what to do with those is a good idea
10 messages were moved here from #mathlib4 > Fixing typos in declarations by David Ang.
I guess anyone has the power to move messages, and for now I'll call this "fixing mathlib" "fixing inconsistencies in mathlib" because I'm aware not everyone wants to use AI for this.

Umm that's a pretty ominous title, I think you'll attract 100% of people reading their inbox page which is probably not what you meant
Edit: it was fixed

Luigi Massacci said:

Since you opened the floodgates of AI assisted fixes

I think Harald Husum started it way before, see PRs
Yeah, I was definitely partly motivated from reviewing their PRs.

/poll What to do with the theories pages:
1) fix the stale references to specific decls / files
2) add a deprecation warning, point to phrasebook

For 2), the idea is that this way it's still available while some of the content is moved to the phrasebook more slowly, but also not confusing newcomers. I have no idea the extent to which 1) suffices to fix the problems in the files.
Argh, I can't edit the message?? Option 3) should have been a note at the bottom, sorry for the formatting mistake
I think that means we should now all massively vote for option 3 :rofl:
I think (2) is great but I think the phrasebook needs to be more comprehensive (which is a good thing!)
Until last night somehow I didn't know the existence of the phrasebook...

As the main maintainer for the phrasebook, I'd like to point out that Verso checks all the code in the phrasebook continues to compile, if we update the Mathlib dependency. In fact, I was going to update to v4.35.0 just now :)
